findings.measured: True peak is +3.0 dBTP, above full scale; expect distortion on playback and after lossy encoding.

steps.text: Put Pro-L 2 last on the master, turn on True Peak Limiting, and set Output Level to −1.0 dB.

other_options.text: Put Adaptive Limiter last on the Stereo Out, turn on True Peak Detection, and set Out Ceiling to −1.0 dB.
Open Pro-L 2's loudness meters and read Integrated and True Peak over the whole song.
Insert Metering › Loudness Meter on the Stereo Out and play the whole song; read the Integrated value.

findings.measured: Integrated loudness is -1.2 LUFS; Spotify would turn it down about 12.8 dB.

steps.text: Lower Pro-L 2's Gain by 2–4 dB and use Unity Gain to compare at matched volume.

other_options.text: Lower Adaptive Limiter's Gain by 2–4 dB and compare at matched volume.
Streaming services turn this down to about −14 LUFS anyway, so the extra limiting only costs punch.

findings.measured: Peak-to-loudness ratio is 4.2 dB; the master is heavily limited.

steps.text: Lower Pro-L 2's Gain by 2–4 dB and use Unity Gain to compare at matched volume.

other_options.text: Lower Adaptive Limiter's Gain by 2–4 dB and compare at matched volume.
On the drum bus, use Pro-C 2 in Punch style with a slower attack (10–30 ms).
In Pro-C 2 on the mix bus, raise Threshold or lengthen Attack until transients come through.

findings.measured: Loudness range is 2.7 LU; there is little contrast between sections.

steps.text: Press A to show automation and draw volume so verses sit 2–3 dB below choruses.

other_options.text: In Pro-C 2 on the mix bus, raise Threshold or lengthen Attack until transients come through.

notes.headline: Your true peak is +3.0 dBTP — this master is clipping above full scale and will distort on playback and after encoding, so pull the ceiling down before anything else.
notes.summary: The balance and mono behaviour of this master are in good shape, but it's pushed far past where it needs to be. True peak reads +3.0 dBTP, which is above full scale: converters and lossy encoders will distort on it. That level of push also shows up as -1.2 LUFS integrated, a peak-to-loudness ratio of 4.2 dB and a loudness range of 2.7 LU — Spotify would turn this down about 12.8 dB anyway, so you're giving up punch and section contrast for loudness nobody will hear.

priorities.title: Get the true peak under full scale
priorities.why: At +3.0 dBTP the file is over the ceiling; that's audible distortion on consumer playback and it gets worse once MP3/AAC encoding adds its own overshoot. This is the one thing here that's wrong regardless of genre.

priorities.title: Back off the limiter
priorities.why: -1.2 LUFS with a 4.2 dB peak-to-loudness ratio means the limiter is doing most of the work. Streaming turns it down about 12.8 dB, so the extra gain only costs you transients — the master will sound smaller than a quieter one at matched volume.

priorities.title: Restore contrast between sections
priorities.why: A loudness range of 2.7 LU means verses and choruses sit at nearly the same level, so the song stops building. Some of this will come back on its own once the limiter is backed off.

listen_for: After setting the Pro-L 2 output to −1.0 dB with True Peak Limiting on, check the loudest section on earbuds or a phone speaker for crackle or grit on vocal and cymbal peaks.
With Unity Gain engaged in Pro-L 2, A/B 2–4 dB less gain and listen to whether kick and snare transients push forward.
Play the whole song and watch the Integrated and True Peak readouts in Pro-L 2's loudness meters to confirm the peak reads under the ceiling end to end.
Listen to a verse into a chorus and ask whether the chorus actually lifts once you've drawn 2–3 dB of volume automation.
strengths: Left/right balance is dead centre at -0.01 dB.
Mono loss is only 0.63 dB, so nothing important collapses on a mono system.
Stereo correlation of 0.744 and low-end correlation of 0.768 are both healthy — the bottom end holds together.

judge.priority_order: Critical true-peak issue (F1) is placed first, followed by the loudness/limiting group (F2+F3) and then the LRA issue (F4), matching severity order in the report.
judge.explains_impact: Each priority states a listening consequence: distortion on playback/encoding for F1, loss of transient punch/perceived size for F2+F3, and lack of build between verse/chorus for F4.
judge.groups_causes: F2 (loudness) and F3 (low PLR) are correctly merged as symptoms of the same over-limiting, while F4 (LRA) is kept separate as a distinct issue about section contrast.
judge.specific: Notes cite exact figures from the report (+3.0 dBTP, -1.2 LUFS, 4.2 dB PLR, 2.7 LU LRA, 12.8 dB Spotify turn-down, 0.744/0.768 correlations) rather than generic advice.
judge.stage_appropriate: Since the stage is master, the notes correctly treat loudness/limiting as a real problem to fix rather than exempting it as they would for a pre-master headroom stage.
judge.faithful: All claims (distortion above full scale, loudness turn-down amount, correlation values, mono loss) match the report; no unsupported causes or contradictions are introduced.
judge.concise: Despite covering four findings, each priority and note is short and purposeful, though the headline and summary repeat the same loudness figures slightly.
